dedupe_keys.name: dlbreach simplified physically based dam and levee breach model version 2016 4 clarkson university

description: DLBreach is a simplified physically-based model of how earthen dams, levees, dikes and barriers erode and fail, developed by Weiming Wu at Clarkson University. The 120-page technical report for version 2016.4, whose opening pages were read on 2026-09-28, covers breaching by overtopping of non-cohesive, cohesive and composite embankments and by piping, routing of breach flow including waves, reservoir storage, spillways and downstream water levels, and non-equilibrium sediment transport, cohesive erosion and headcut migration, and lists model parameters and outputs. It reports tests against dam breach cases by failure type with overall performance statistics, and against levee and barrier breaches such as the Zwin channel dike, Mecox Inlet in New York, the Yahekou fuse plug dam and the Sutter Bypass levee. Coverage is generic, for any earthen embankment. The report is free to read; a disclaimer asks for engineering expertise, no licence is stated, and how to obtain the program was not read. Caveats: the programming language and input formats were not read, and version 2016.4 may have been superseded. It supports dam and levee failure studies, such as producing breach outflow hydrographs for downstream flood mapping and emergency planning of reservoirs and flood defences. No related embankment breach model record is catalogued.
